lines.text: What if a ceiling in space was really a blur in the measuring tape?
Physicist Nithin Sivadas led a Nature study with U A F coauthor Doğacan Öztürk.
Today, NASA's Wind spacecraft orbits L one, nine hundred thirty thousand miles sunward.
The team paired one minute solar wind observations with polar cap responses from nineteen ninety five through twenty nineteen.
But the signal changes on its trip.
Uncertainty in arrival time, strength, location, and evolution can match a measurement with the wrong response.
Simulate those mismatches, and a saturated-looking curve appears.
So the researchers calibrated the uncertainty.
The corrected average relation rose linearly through the observed limit of fifteen millivolts per meter.
Near twenty five, projected geomagnetic response reaches roughly twice the older saturated estimate. But that is extrapolated, not observed, and not doubled damage.
Physical saturation could still appear beyond the data.
And no operational A I forecast was tested.
A flexible model can fit the biased curve, but can't recover information the measurement blurred.
Space weather can affect grids, G P S, aircraft, and satellites. But this is no forecast, current alert, or Alaska data set.
A model can follow the ribbon. It can't restore what the measurement lost.

Transcript:
What if a ceiling in space was really a blur in the measuring tape?
Physicist Nithin Sivadas led a Nature study with U A F coauthor Doğacan Öztürk.
Today, NASA's Wind spacecraft orbits L one, nine hundred thirty thousand miles sunward.
The team paired one minute solar wind observations with polar cap responses from nineteen ninety five through twenty nineteen.
But the signal changes on its trip.
Uncertainty in arrival time, strength, location, and evolution can match a measurement with the wrong response.
Simulate those mismatches, and a saturated-looking curve appears.
So the researchers calibrated the uncertainty.
The corrected average relation rose linearly through the observed limit of fifteen millivolts per meter.
Then comes the test.
Evidence stops at fifteen.
Near twenty five, projected geomagnetic response reaches roughly twice the older saturated estimate. But that is extrapolated, not observed, and not doubled damage.
Physical saturation could still appear beyond the data.
And no operational A I forecast was tested.
A flexible model can fit the biased curve, but can't recover information the measurement blurred.
Space weather can affect grids, G P S, aircraft, and satellites. But this is no forecast, current alert, or Alaska data set.
The apparent ceiling moved.
The evidence boundary did not.
